security_findings.finding: _remove suppresses every Docker removal RuntimeError/OSError and the finally block discards the name without verifying deletion. Missing containers and daemon/removal failures are indistinguishable, so failed cleanup can leave a sandbox untracked.
security_findings.recommendation: Track removal outcome, distinguish missing container from control failure, retain/report unresolved names without learner data, fail closed or reconcile before further work; add a mocked removal-failure regression.

security_findings.finding: Rootless prototype relies on per-process rlimits and tmpfs bounds rather than aggregate cgroup memory/PID accounting and host-wide resource budgets. The recorded installed runtime is older than the reviewed upstream release.
security_findings.recommendation: Maintain a dedicated audited runtime and host-level quotas/monitoring before public exposure. Current tests cannot certify sandbox security.

security_findings.finding: MLE remains accepted in protocol and summary vocabularies, while this harness intentionally emits RE for ambiguous allocation failures and has no trustworthy aggregate accounting. Do not describe MLE as an exercised live result.
security_findings.recommendation: Document reserved/unsupported measured memory verdict semantics; only enable precise MLE with trustworthy runtime accounting.

consolidation.reason: Worker reselects a fixed safe vocabulary and discards arbitrary runner summary; merging would blur the independent sanitation boundary. Wording differences are not competing implementations.
Host holds expected answers and credentials; sandbox receives only source and selected inputs. Feature grouping must not collapse this security boundary.
A single shared implementation is explicitly copied into the runtime image; no duplicate source file exists in Git.

consolidation.decision: keep boundary; cross-service consistency validation useful
consolidation.reason: Same public problem contract appears at two trust/runtime boundaries. Shared heavy imports into judge would be worse; a serialization contract or integration check can catch drift.

unknowns: No current runtime, container, hosted CI or exploitation observation was performed by this subreview. Parent owns actual validation.
Not an independent sandbox penetration test or artifact provenance attestation.

remediation.status: implemented in working tree; parent owns commit/live integration
behavior: Failed Docker rm uses one bounded successful container-list query to establish absence.
Unresolved names remain tracked and runner readiness is revoked; _container fails with a sanitized error instead of returning a successful response.
Cancellation attempts all tracked names, retains failures for a later cancellation attempt and emits a controlled error after best effort.
Pending cleanup prevents the same instance from regaining readiness through preflight.
Worker stops heartbeats and further job claims when readiness is revoked, completes the current leased job with its controlled verdict and triggers cancellation without blocking forever.
limited_process cancellation callback may ignore a False return, but _remove immediately revokes readiness and retains the name; _container finally retries bounded removal and checks its outcome.

validation.live_sandbox: not run by child; root owns integration

remaining_limitations: API capabilities use the existing 60-second heartbeat freshness window. This patch stops renewals; it does not add an immediate server-side revocation endpoint.
An already in-flight heartbeat can finish during a concurrent readiness transition; there are no further renewals or claims after the worker observes it.
Unresolved container names remain in process memory and sanitized operator error, not a durable reconciliation store; production orphan reconciliation remains future work.
